title: Only my programs may connect
description:
Make a local server check that a client knows a secret before serving it, without sending the secret.

```
server sends challenge 8f3a...
client answers HMAC(secret, challenge)
server: answer correct -> connected
another client with a wrong secret -> refused
replaying an old answer -> refused (new challenge each time)
```
hints: Constant time: `return ((a ^ b) == 0);` compares all bits at once; for byte arrays, OR together the XOR of every pair (lesson 5.05).
Where the secret lives matters as much as the protocol: a file only the user can read, or the Windows credential store.
requirements: A random challenge per connection (`std::random_device` and `std::mt19937_64` are fine here).
The answer is a keyed hash of the challenge; use any simple keyed hash for the exercise (for example FNV-1a over secret + challenge), and note that a real program would use HMAC-SHA256.
stretch: Also check the client's process id against an allow list (`GetNamedPipeClientProcessId`).
